answer: Commit-reveal work receipts hide the output hash until the epoch closes, and each disagreement among reviewing peers dilutes the payout by 20%, so a farm that submits one answer behind 60 identities collects 60 diluted shares of the same work. With five reviewers per task the dilution curve makes a shared answer worth 0.8^5 of a solo one, and the dune of duplicate receipts stops paying. The fable that volume beats quality dies at the first close, and no plume of aliases fixes it.
